Priya to review SOC2 docs and schedule security follow-up call (by 2026-03-05)

Diego Alvarez: Run 1k-request throughput benchmark on Redwood Dedicated using customer's prompts (due 2026-03-04)

header: Date: 2026-02-26 15:00 UTC | Duration: 46 min | Attendees: Samira Khan, Diego Alvarez, Maya Patel, Evan Chu, Priya Rao
summary: Redwood AE+SE ran a migration-focused demo for CleverChat covering parity mapping from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood API. Key discussion points: API request/response parity, streaming and function-calling differences, embeddings and reranking behavior, Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs, and security/KMS/VPC requirements. Action items: share parity spreadsheet, run throughput bench on Dedicated, follow up on SOC2/KMS. Customer is on a 6-week evaluation timeline and is most sensitive to latency and data residency.
transcript:
[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Samira from Redwood, I have Diego with me - he's our solutions engineer. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Maya: Hi Maya here, VP Product at CleverChat.
[00:10] Evan: Evan, platform engineering.
[00:12] Priya: Priya, security.
[00:14] Diego: Great, thanks. The plan is a focused migration demo, parity mapping - how requests from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together map to Redwood. We'll show the Console, API, and Optimize tips.
[00:30] Maya: High level: we use OpenAI for chat/generation and Together for lower-cost batch inference, and Anthropic for some safety models. We want a one-platform approach but need parity.
[00:42] Samira: Totally. Can you share your success criteria? Latency, cost, and data residency I assume?
[00:48] Maya: Yep, latency sub-300ms for 512 tokens for core path, embeddings identical outputs-ish, and SOC2/KMS for compliance.
[00:56] Priya: Also audit logs and SSO - we use Okta with SAML.
[00:59] Diego: Good notes. Quick note: Redwood's API mirrors a familiar shape - you can send messages or completions, streaming, function calling is supported. There are naming differences though, e.g., model ids and some param names.
[01:15] Evan: How much work is the mapping? We have ~25 endpoints in our microservices calling OpenAI.
[01:20] Samira: We generally create a parity mapping spreadsheet and a Postman collection/sample lib. For simple cases it's a few lines change - model param, streaming flag. For function calling, we support the same call flow but the event payload has slight field names. We'll send the mapping.
[01:40] Diego: I'll demo a live mapping from an OpenAI chat request to Redwood's API.
[01:46] [02:05] Diego: (screen) Here's an OpenAI payload: messages, max_tokens, temperature. On Redwood you call /v1/generate with messages and model. We map max_tokens to max_output_tokens, temperature same. Some customers call stop sequences differently - we support both via stop or stop_tokens param.
[02:30] Maya: Any gotchas with streaming? Our product uses streaming partial responses heavily.
[02:35] Diego: Streaming works the same; we stream token events. Small difference: we include a prefix event that carries model metadata, and the SSE format is slightly different. Most SDKs handle it.
[02:50] Evan: Are there any rate limiting semantics we should be aware of?
[02:54] Samira: We expose rate limits per API key and per route, and can do burst policies. For Dedicated customers we can bump limits or use internal pooling.
[03:06] Priya: Security - can you talk KMS integration and key rotation?
[03:10] Diego: Yes; Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM. You can bring keys via KMS connectors. Rotation is supported but needs coordination; we can share our runbook.
[03:22] Priya: And audit logs?
[03:24] Samira: Full request/response metadata logging is available for Dedicated/Private, with redaction options for PII. We also have SAML SSO and RBAC at the route/token level.
[03:36] Maya: About embeddings - we use OpenAI embeddings for semantic search, dimension 1536. Anthropic we sometimes use for reranking. How does Redwood handle this?
[03:45] Diego: We support multiple embedding models with outputs that are compatible size-wise - 1536, 1024, etc. For reranking we recommend using our reranker API which accepts embeddings and scores or you can replicate the same dot-prod logic. There are small float differences; we add a note in the parity sheet for normalization.
[04:05] Evan: Any tooling to detect model regressions?
[04:07] Samira: Yes Optimize has quality monitoring and evaluation sets. You can push prompt sets and we flag regressions vs baseline.
[04:16] Maya: Demo time?
[04:18] Diego: Sure. I'm going to show a chat example then an embeddings flow.
[04:25] [05:00] Diego: (typing) Here's the OpenAI chat example converted to Redwood. Notice the header X-Redwood-Client and model name redwood/gpt-{size}. Function calling: we attach function schemas, Redwood will return a call with name and arguments similar to OpenAI but the argument envelope sometimes differs, so you may need a tiny adapter.
[05:30] Maya: That adapter work - small lambda?
[05:33] Diego: Usually 10-20 lines; we provide reference adapters in Node/Python.
[05:40] Priya: What about Together models for cost savings, how do you handle fallback?
[05:44] Samira: Smart routing: you can set policy to route cost-sensitive requests to Together-compatible models and critical low-latency ones to Dedicated high-perf models. Also automatic fallback if capacity is constrained.
[06:00] Evan: For on-prem or VPC, does your control plane still see telemetry?
[06:04] Diego: For Private deployments you can opt into telemetry; otherwise control plane interactions are minimized and logs stay in customer infra if using the on-prem package.
[06:15] Maya: Can we see the Console for routing rules and Optimize suggestions?
[06:19] Diego: Yep - switching to Console. (screen) Here's per-route latency and cost breakdown, you can set batching thresholds and suggested quantization per model. Optimize suggests config for batching and quantization based on your prompt length distribution.
[06:45] Maya: That quantization suggestion is useful.
[06:48] Diego: We also expose a model catalog where we mark models as Redwood-verified with perf profiles.
[06:52] Priya: Back to security: how do you guarantee data residency for EU customers?
[06:56] Samira: You can pin a region and deploy Dedicated capacity in a particular cloud region - data residency is enforced by routing policy and storage location. For Private we run everything in your VPC.
[07:10] Evan: Benchmarks - can you run sample prompts at scale?
[07:13] Diego: Yes, if you share sample prompt set and request distribution we can run throughput bench on Dedicated or Hosted; for realistic KV cache patterns we need sequence-length distribution.
[07:25] Maya: We have a 30% prefix reuse pattern which should help caching.
[07:29] Diego: That's great - Optimize will call that out and suggest caching policy.
[07:35] [08:00] Samira: Let's walk through a migration plan: phase 1 parity mapping and adapter work, phase 2 pilot with Dedicated capacity for a critical route, phase 3 expand and cut over. Typical 4-8 week pilot.
[08:20] Maya: Timeline fits our 6-week evaluation window.
[08:24] Evan: Any contractual/commitment ask for Dedicated?
[08:28] Samira: Dedicated has reserved capacity contracts but we can start with a short pilot on burst or a smaller reserved commit. Pricing will be in the doc.
[08:38] Priya: Can you share SOC2 certs and pen test report?
[08:41] Samira: Yes, Samira: we'll send SOC2, penetration test summary, and our security runbook.
[08:48] Maya: Quick Q: embeddings drift - if outputs differ slightly, will our search quality degrade?
[08:52] Diego: There can be small numeric differences; the recommended path is to reindex with Redwood embeddings or use an emb-sim layer that normalizes. We have a recommended migration recipe in the sheet.
[09:08] Maya: Ok. Anything else on function calling?
[09:12] Diego: One note - for hollowed function call usage patterns we support streaming of partial function argument chunks so large schemas don't blow up latency.
[09:24] Priya: Regarding SSO/SCIM, do you support automatic user provisioning?
[09:28] Samira: Yes SCIM provisioning is supported for Enterprise accounts.
[09:31] Evan: Are there any OpenAI/Anthropic license or TOS differences we should be aware of when changing endpoints?
[09:36] Samira: Not typically - you'll need to review any existing licensing clauses, but Redwood provides an API surface; model licensing depends on model vendor for some open models.
[09:48] Maya: Let's talk benchmarks - can you give a sample result?
[09:52] Diego: For a 768-token prompt on a Dedicated gpus we see p95 latencies around 180-220ms depending on model; batch size and KV cache make a big difference. I can share a benchmark sheet.
[10:12] Evan: Any quirks around prompt length and tokenization?
[10:16] Diego: We use UTF-8 and our token counters align with typical BPE tokenizers; you might see off-by-one counts, we include a tokenization preview in the Console.
[10:30] Maya: Security follow-up: Priya wants to schedule a deep-dive.
[10:34] Priya: Yes, I'd like a SOC2 walkthrough and the KMS architecture.
[10:38] Samira: We'll set up a 30-min security call next week.
[10:44] Maya: Pricing - any ballpark for Dedicated pilot?
[10:47] Samira: Pilot pricing varies; I'll include a pilot estimate in the sheet. For Hosted usage pricing per token applies. For Dedicated we can do monthly commit tiers.
[11:00] Evan: Ok. Anything about data retention?
[11:03] Diego: Retention is configurable; defaults differ for Hosted vs Dedicated. Private can be indefinite per your retention policy.
[11:12] Maya: Great. Quick recap of next steps?
[11:15] Samira: I'll send parity mapping sheet, Postman collection, pricing, and SOC2 docs. Diego will run bench. Priya will confirm KMS and region needs and we'll schedule sec call.
[11:28] [11:40] Maya: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[11:43] Evan: Thanks.
[11:45] Priya: Thanks.
[11:47] Samira: Thanks all, we'll follow up.
[11:50] Speaker 1: (end)
